dod.item: Autonomy is a versioned policy row carrying approver kind and typed conditions plus expiry; it defaults off, is revoked automatically when a condition fails, and a change to it requires an approval decision rather than a plain write.

evidence.quote: /// This tenant has opted out for this action; the call runs without one.

subjects.detail: §9.3/D34 require auto-merge to be an approval_policy row with `approver_kind='auto'` and typed conditions — consecutive green runs, revert count, path scope, independent reviewer, expiry — all tenant configuration, and the policy change itself a gated change. The implemented policy has exactly two fields, `approval` (required|waived) and `self_approval`, and `waives()` returns true for any action whose row says `waived`. There are no conditions, no expiry, no revert or reviewer inputs, no version dimension, and `approval_policies.set` is an ordinary `write` action, so the policy is not itself gated. A single holder of `approvals:write` can permanently switch a destructive gate off.

evidence.quote: /// This tenant has opted out for this action; the call runs without one.

packages.title: Earned auto-merge is replaced by an unconditional policy waiver

dod.item: Self-approval is unconditional: the decision writer refuses a decision whose approver is the gate's requester/executor, with no policy row able to relax it. Any historical exception is an explicit, audited override rather than a stored permission.

subjects.detail: P4 and §5.4 state flatly that the executor/assignee/requester cannot approve the gate that judges their work. The policy model adds a second opt-out, `self_approval` (forbidden|allowed), and the decision writer consults `allows_self_approval` for the gate's action. Setting `allowed` therefore makes the requester a valid approver for their own gate, so dual control and P4 are tenant-waivable configuration rather than invariants.

dod.item: phase_progress counts only status='approved' artefacts and status='live' contracts (matching advance_phase_tx), so a phase reported `evidenced` is one the gate would also close.

subjects.detail: `phase_progress` builds `artifact_phases` from every architecture_artifact row the snapshot carries without testing `status`, and picks one contract per (project, phase) by recency without testing `status`; "evidenced" is then computed from those sets. The console therefore reports progress under a rule that contradicts `advance_phase_tx`, which only accepts an `approved` artefact and a `live` contract.
